header.userPrompt:
Fix an infinite recursion bug in the ZIO 1 stubbing helpers.

File: effects/zio1/src/main/scala/sttp/client4/impl/zio/SttpClientStubbingBase.scala

`AbstractClientStubbing` defines `val monad = new RIOMonadAsyncError[R]` (line ~20). In `StreamClientStubbing.proxy` (line ~101) and `WebSocketStreamClientStubbing.proxy` (line ~120), the anonymous backend classes define `def monad: MonadError[RIO[R, *]] = monad`. Inside the anonymous class, `monad` resolves to the method itself, so calling `monad` on the proxied backend recurses forever (StackOverflowError).

Acceptance criteria:
1. Both proxy backends' `monad` return the outer trait's `RIOMonadAsyncError` instance (e.g. via a self-alias or a qualified reference such as `AbstractClientStubbing.this.monad` / a local val captured before the anonymous class). Pick the simplest, clearest form.
2. Check whether the ZIO 2 module (effects/zio/...) has the same pattern; fix it there too if so.
3. Add a regression test in the zio1 module's test sources (follow existing test layout) that calls `monad` on the proxied backend (both stream and websocket-stream variants) and verifies it does not recurse and returns a usable MonadError.
4. Compile and run the relevant tests, e.g. `sbt "testScoped 3 JVM"` scoped to the zio1 project (find the exact project id in build.sbt, e.g. `zio1JVM/test` / `zio1/test`), and for Scala 2.13 as well.

Keep the change minimal.
